message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of some of the most famous American composers—across classical, popular, and contemporary genres—who have left a lasting mark on U.S. music history:

| Composer | Era / Genre | Notable Works / Contributions |
|----------|-------------|--------------------------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Classical/Popular crossover | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, *Porgy & Bess* |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900‑1990) | Classical | “Appalachian Spring,” “Fanfare for the Common Man,” “Rodeo” |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Classical/Showtunes | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, *On the Town* |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film score | Scores for *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park*, *Harry Potter* |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalism | *Einstein on the Beach*, *Glassworks*, *Koyaanisqatsi* |
| **Ludwig van Beethoven** (not American) – *[Just a reminder]* | Classical | *Symphony No. 9*, *Moonlight Sonata* |
| **Stephen Sondheim** (1920‑2021) | Musical theatre | *Sweeney Todd*, *Into the Woods*, *Company* |
| **Bobby McFerrin** (born 1950) | Jazz/Pop | “Don’t Worry, Be Happy,” *The Art of the Song* |
| **John Philip Sousa** (1854‑1932) | March music | “The Stars and Stripes Forever,” “The Liberty Bell” |
| **Charles Ives** (1874‑1954) | Experimental | *The Unanswered Question*, *The Swimmer* |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910‑1981) | Classical | “Adagio for Strings,” *Knoxville: Summer of 1915* |
| **Duke Ellington** (1899‑1974) | Jazz | “Take the A Train,” *Mood Indigo*, *Black, Brown, and Beige* |
| **Miles Davis** (1926‑1991) | Jazz | *Kind of Blue*, *Bitches Brew*, *Sketches of Spain* |
| **John Adams** (born 1947) | Contemporary classical | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine* |
| **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | Minimalism | *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains* |
| **John Cage** (1912‑1992) | Experimental | *4′33″*, *Sonatas and Interludes* |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Classical/Showtunes | *West Side Story*, *Candide*, *On the Town* |
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Classical/Popular crossover | *Rhapsody in Blue*, *An American in Paris*, *Porgy & Bess* |

### How to Use This List
- **Research**: Each name is a gateway to a rich body of work. Look up their most influential pieces for deeper study.
- **Listening**: Many of these works are available on streaming platforms; start with the most iconic titles listed.
- **Education**: If you’re studying music theory or composition, these composers offer diverse styles—from classical symphonies to jazz improvisation and minimalist patterns.

Feel free to ask if you’d like more details on any particular composer or genre!
